study_identification.title: Microstructural mapping of neural pathways in Alzheimer's disease using macrostructure-informed normative tractometry
study_identification.doi: Not explicitly stated in the article

study_characteristics.study_objective: To propose a novel macrostructure-informed normative tractometry (MINT) framework using a variational autoencoder (VAE) to jointly model white matter microstructural measures and bundle geometry variations, and to investigate how WM microstructure and macrostructure are jointly altered in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia in two multisite cohorts from North America and India.

dataset_name.answer: ADNI Phase 3; NIMHANS (Bangalore, India); TractoInferno (for pretraining)

hc_n.answer: ADNI: 447 CN (analyzed cross-sectionally); NIMHANS: 123 CN; TractoInferno: 198 (pretraining dataset for VAE model)

hc_age.answer: ADNI Total: mean 74.13 ± SD 7.93 years; NIMHANS Total: mean 67.25 ± SD 7.86 years; TractoInferno: demographics including age and sex are available in reference 38 (Poulin et al., 2022)

hc_sex.answer: ADNI Total: Male 349 (47.81%); NIMHANS Total: Male 177 (58.61%); TractoInferno: sex information available in reference 38

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: ADNI: ADNI preprocessing pipeline detailed in references 4, 15 including denoising (local PCA, DiPy), Gibbs ringing removal (DiPy), susceptibility-induced distortion/eddy current/motion correction (FSL topup and eddy_cuda), bias field inhomogeneity correction (MRtrix dwibiascorrect). NIMHANS: Similar pipeline to ADNI including denoising (local PCA, DiPy), Gibbs ringing removal (DiPy), susceptibility-induced distortion/eddy current/motion correction (FSL topup and eddy_cuda, Synb0-DisCo for Siemens), bias field inhomogeneity correction (MRtrix dwibiascorrect); DTI fitting (non-linear least-squares); fiber orientation reconstruction (RUMBA-SD with contextual enhancement); tractography (particle filtering tracking, 8 seeds per voxel, step size 0.2mm, angular threshold 30°). TractoInferno: Constrained spherical deconvolution and deterministic tracking for whole-brain tractograms. Bundle segmentation: DiPy's autocalibrated RecoBundles method using HCP-842 atlas for 30 WM bundles.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Bundles with fewer than 96 streamlines were removed. The study mentions that UF and IFOF bundles were not well reconstructed in all subjects across all protocols, which affected downstream harmonization and statistical analysis (Section S5).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization applied to along-tract bundle profiles. ComBat is a 'location and scale' model where each measurement is affected by additive and multiplicative effects of scanner and protocol, estimated using empirical Bayes. ComBat was run for each of 30 bundles and 9 features (5 MAE measures and 4 DTI measures), pooling information across 100 segments per bundle, with age and sex modeled as covariates. ComBat parameters were estimated on training set (CN only) to prevent data leakage, then applied to test set (CN, MCI, and dementia). Python implementation of ComBat (https://github.com/Jfortin1/neuroCombat) was used. ADNI data were collected using 7 acquisition protocols (S31, S55, S127, P33, P36, GE36, GE54) from 3 scanner vendors with varying numbers of gradient directions. The study analyzed ADNI and NIMHANS separately as they were recruited from different geographic regions with different demographics and cognitive assessments in different languages.

modeling_method.answer: Deep Learning (Variational Autoencoder with 1D convolutional layers, ConvVAE)

software_tool.answer: Custom MINT framework; DiPy; PyTorch (implied from VAE implementation); Code and pretrained model available at https://github.com/wendyfyx/MINT

response_variable.answer: FA (Fractional Anisotropy); MD (Mean Diffusivity); RD (Radial Diffusivity); AxD (Axial Diffusivity); 3D streamline coordinates (for macrostructure/shape). All DTI metrics were projected onto 30 white matter bundles in native space. Streamlines resampled to 128 equidistant points with 7 input features (x, y, z, FA, MD, RD, AxD).

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex were modeled as covariates in ComBat harmonization. Scanner/protocol effects were removed through ComBat's empirical Bayes estimation of additive and multiplicative effects. The VAE model itself learns patterns of micro- and macrostructural variation in healthy controls without explicit predictor modeling in the network architecture.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study appropriately handles multiple types of nuisance structure: (1) Site/scanner/protocol effects through ComBat harmonization with empirical Bayes estimation of additive and multiplicative effects; (2) Age and sex effects preserved as biological covariates in ComBat; (3) Crossing fiber effects addressed through joint modeling of microstructure and macrostructure in the VAE; (4) Protocol heterogeneity across 7 ADNI protocols and 2 NIMHANS scanners handled via harmonization; (5) Data leakage prevention by estimating ComBat on training set only.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: ComBat is a 'location and scale' model, where we assume that each measurement is affected by the additive and multiplicative effects of the scanner and protocol, estimated using an empirical Bayes method. Covariates can also be specified in ComBat to preserve the known biological variability across subjects (eg, age and sex). In this study, ComBat was run for each of the 30 bundles and nine features, by pooling information across 100 segments of each bundle, with age and sex modeled as covariates... To prevent data leakage, we estimated ComBat parameters on bundle profiles created from the training set for both cohorts previously used in fine-tuning. The training set contained only CN subjects, so the diagnosis was not included in the ComBat model during training.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study uses a split-sample validation approach within each cohort. For both ADNI and NIMHANS, CN participants were split into 35%/15%/50% for training/validation/testing. The validation set (15%) was used to adjust fine-tuning parameters and inspect reconstruction quality. This represents validation on non-independent data from the same domain (same cohort, same acquisition protocols).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: For both the ADNI and NIMHANS datasets, data from the CN participants were split into independent subsets of size 35%/15%/50% for training/validation/testing... The validation set was used to adjust the model's fine-tuning parameters, such as batch size and number of training steps, and inspect the reconstruction quality.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study uses a held-out test set (50% of CN plus all MCI and dementia cases) within each cohort for final evaluation. However, this is technically from the same cohort/domain as the training data, though it is an independent split. The test set contains 226 CN subjects from ADNI and 62 from NIMHANS that were not used in training. This represents same-domain independent validation, but the independence is achieved through data splitting rather than using a completely separate dataset.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Data from participants with MCI or dementia were concatenated with the 50% CN subjects to create the test set. The test set contained a large percentage of CN subjects - 226 subjects from ADNI and 62 from NIMHANS - to better estimate group difference statistics from the resulting deviation scores.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study validates across different domains in multiple ways: (1) Transfer learning approach where a model pretrained on TractoInferno dataset (198 subjects from 6 studies) is fine-tuned on ADNI and NIMHANS separately; (2) Cross-cohort validation between ADNI (North American) and NIMHANS (Indian) cohorts with different demographics, scanners, and protocols; (3) Comparison of findings across cohorts to assess generalizability. The ADNI cohort (mean age 74.13±7.93) was significantly older than NIMHANS (67.25±7.86), and they had different proportions of diagnoses, different scanners, and different cognitive assessment batteries.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: In our study, this pretraining dataset consisted of 198 single-shell dMRI volumes already preprocessed from the publicly available TractoInferno training dataset... The pretrained VAE model was fine-tuned on 30 bundles from the subjects in the training set, in each cohort, for 5000 steps. We did not pool the training data in ADNI and NIMHANS together in this step, to simulate the scenario where sites cannot share raw data, but can still share bundle profiles computed from their own fine-tuned model... Comparing the two cohorts, ADNI (74.13 ± 7.93) was significantly older than the NIMHANS cohort (67.25 ± 7.86); t(1030) = 12.72, p = 1.5 × 10^-34. The proportions of diagnosis were significantly different across the two cohorts.

clinical_dataset.answer: ADNI Phase 3 (MCI and dementia participants); NIMHANS (MCI and dementia participants)

clinical_groups_age.answer: ADNI Total (includes CN, MCI, Dementia): 74.13±7.93 years; NIMHANS Total (includes CN, MCI, Dementia): 67.25±7.86 years. Specific age breakdowns by diagnostic group not provided in demographics table, but total cohort ages are reported. ADNI protocols range: S31 (72.03±8.51), S55 (74.41±7.93), S127 (73.66±7.58), P33 (75.74±7.68), P36 (73.14±6.93), GE36 (72.24±7.15), GE45 (76.11±8.06). deviation_metric.answer: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) between reconstructed and original data from VAE for five features: MAE-Shape (from 3D coordinates), MAE-FA, MAE-MD, MAE-RD, MAE-AxD. MAE calculated for each of 100 along-tract segments. Higher MAE indicates greater deviation from normative patterns learned by the VAE.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear regression models fitted for each of 100 segments in 30 bundles with harmonized diffusion metrics as dependent variable and diagnosis (DX), age, and sex as independent variables (MAE ~ Age + Sex + DX, M ~ Age + Sex + DX). CN group used as reference for MCI and dementia comparisons. Separate analyses for ADNI and NIMHANS cohorts. FDR correction applied to 3000 tests across whole brain. Additional analysis using linear mixed models for merged cohorts with cohort as random effect and age, sex, DX as fixed effects. Dementia vs MCI comparisons also conducted with MCI as reference. Partial Spearman rank-order correlations computed between cognitive assessment scores and bundle profile features, removing effects of age and sex. ADNI: CDRsb, ADAS13, MMSE. NIMHANS: SMIR, SMDR, WLDR. Q-Q plots used to rank sensitivity of different dMRI metrics to dementia.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study found consistent patterns of widespread microstructural and macrostructural white matter abnormalities in MCI and dementia compared to healthy controls in both ADNI and NIMHANS cohorts, with MD and RD being most sensitive to dementia, and demonstrated that joint modeling of microstructure and macrostructure using MINT can help disentangle disease effects from confounds like crossing fibers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: In two independent cohorts (ADNI N=730, NIMHANS N=302), the study identified widespread white matter abnormalities in MCI and dementia with strongest effects in temporal lobe pathways (ILF, UF, AF), posterior regions (OPT, OR, posterior MdLF and EMC), and corpus callosum (forceps major). All three diffusivity measures (MD, RD, AxD) were elevated in both dementia and MCI compared to controls, with MD and RD showing the strongest associations. A paradoxical fan-shaped pattern was observed in projection pathways where DTI-FA was higher in proximal parts (near deep nuclei) and lower in distal parts (near cortex) in dementia/MCI, likely due to crossing fibers at corona radiata/centrum semiovale. This pattern was mirrored in MAE-Shape, suggesting that apparent FA changes may reflect macrostructural alterations rather than true microstructural degeneration. After accounting for macrostructure through MINT, MAE-FA showed fewer significant group differences than DTI-FA. For ADNI cohort, both DTI and MAE diffusivity measures showed similar associations with CDRsb. For NIMHANS cohort, MAE diffusivity measures (especially MAE-MD and MAE-RD) showed stronger negative correlations with WLDR in more bundles than DTI measures, particularly in posterior/temporal association pathways (EMC, ILF, MdLF), posterior projection pathways (FPT, OPT, OR), and corpus callosum. MAE-Shape showed significant positive correlation with CDRsb and negative correlation with WLDR in multiple bundles. Q-Q plots revealed that of all metrics, MD ranked highest in sensitivity to dementia, followed by RD, AxD, and FA. ComBat harmonization successfully aligned bundle profiles across 7 ADNI protocols and 2 NIMHANS scanners while preserving biological effects of age, sex, and diagnosis. Effect sizes were generally larger and more significant in ADNI than NIMHANS, likely due to larger sample size and age differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Study limitations include: (1) Single-shell dMRI acquisitions with relatively low b-values limit reconstruction of some key bundles like fornix and cingulum using automated methods, despite their importance in early AD changes. (2) Some bundles (UF, IFOF) were not well reconstructed across all protocols, affecting harmonization and statistical analysis. (3) Only baseline cross-sectional scans from ADNI were analyzed, although longitudinal data are available. (4) ADNI and NIMHANS cohorts had significantly different demographics (age, diagnosis proportions) and used different cognitive assessment batteries in different languages, limiting direct comparisons. (5) Confounders such as education and lifestyle factors not available for NIMHANS cohort. (6) Historical clinical definitions of AD used rather than recent biological definitions based on biomarkers. (7) Tractography systematically produces false positive streamlines, limiting which bundles could be reliably analyzed. (8) Partial volume effects from CSF near ventricles (e.g., forceps major) may affect MD interpretation as atrophy rather than microstructural change. (9) The study did not examine relationships with amyloid and tau measures. (10) Sample size differences between cohorts (ADNI larger) affected statistical power and model performance, particularly for MINT macrostructure encoding.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study introduces MINT as a novel framework that jointly models WM microstructure and macrostructure using deep learning. Key innovations include: (1) Use of 1D convolutional VAE to model streamline-level sequential dependencies and whole-brain fiber geometry; (2) Transfer learning approach with pretraining on TractoInferno and fine-tuning on target cohorts; (3) Joint statistical modeling of micro- and macrostructure to attribute variance to appropriate sources; (4) Demonstration that metrics describing diffusion along principal axon direction (FA, AxD) are more susceptible to crossing fibers and macrostructural confounds than MD and RD; (5) Resolution of paradoxical FA patterns in projection pathways through macrostructure modeling; (6) Bundle-wise ComBat harmonization of 9 features across 100 segments per bundle; (7) Prevention of data leakage by estimating harmonization parameters only on training CN subjects; (8) Ranking of DTI metrics by dementia sensitivity using Q-Q plots; (9) Validation of findings across two demographically distinct cohorts from different continents; (10) The framework can produce reconstructions for any collection of streamlines during inference, offering flexibility for whole-brain analysis. Future directions include: incorporating multi-compartment diffusion metrics (e.g., free water) to better account for partial volume effects; examining relationships with AD biomarkers (amyloid, tau); analyzing longitudinal data; assessing relationships with specific neuropsychological domains (language, memory, executive function); investigating education and lifestyle factors in NIMHANS cohort.

general_notes.general_notes:
This study represents an important methodological advance in tractometry by proposing MINT (Macrostructure-Informed Normative Tractometry), which uses deep learning (specifically a VAE with 1D convolutional layers) to jointly model WM microstructure and macrostructure. The key innovation is addressing the long-standing confound in DTI analysis where apparent microstructural changes (especially in FA) may actually reflect macrostructural alterations or crossing fiber geometry. The study demonstrates this through the 'paradoxical' fan-shaped pattern in projection pathways where DTI-FA is higher (not lower) in dementia/MCI in proximal regions, which corresponds to lower MAE-Shape deviations, suggesting the FA changes reflect geometry rather than degeneration. The pretrained model is publicly available (https://github.com/wendyfyx/MINT), promoting reproducibility. The study uses rigorous harmonization with careful attention to data leakage prevention. The validation across two demographically and geographically distinct cohorts (North American ADNI, Indian NIMHANS) strengthens generalizability despite differences in age, scanners, protocols, and cognitive assessments. The ADNI dataset includes 7 different acquisition protocols from 3 scanner vendors, representing realistic multi-site heterogeneity. TractoInferno pretraining dataset contains 198 subjects from 6 studies with single-shell dMRI around b=1000 s/mm². The 30 white matter bundles analyzed include 12 association bundles (bilateral AF, EMC, IFOF, ILF, MdLF, UF), 8 projection bundles (bilateral CST, FPT, OPT, OR), 3 commissural bundles (CC_ForcepsMajor, CC_ForcepsMinor, CCMid), 6 brainstem bundles (bilateral MLF, ML, STT), and 1 cerebellar bundle (V). Bundle profiles created at 100 along-tract segments aligned across subjects using BUAN framework. The VAE architecture: encoder with 4 1D SepConv layers (15 kernel, 32/64/128/256 channels), decoder with 3 layers (15 kernel, 128/96/64 channels), 464,408 total parameters, trained with ELBO loss and cyclical annealing on KL divergence. Pretraining: 24,000 steps on 100+ million streamlines from TractoInferno, batch size 512 with replacement. Fine-tuning: 5000 steps per cohort. Input: 128 equidistant points per streamline, 7 features (x,y,z,FA,MD,RD,AxD), unit sphere normalization for coordinates, min-max scaling for DTI metrics to [-1,1]. Random flipping augmentation enforces flip-independence. Asymmetric encoder-decoder encourages robust representations while reducing parameters. Clinical measures used: ADNI (CDRsb 0.97±1.9, ADAS13 16.28±8.26, MMSE 27.99±2.91), NIMHANS (WLDR 3.61±3.12, SMIR 7.3±3.59, SMDR 5.12±4.3). For ADNI, diagnosis based on clinical assessments including CDR and MMSE. For NIMHANS, diagnosis according to NIA-AA criteria and CDR where CDR=0.5 is MCI and CDR=1 is dementia. Supplementary materials show detailed visualizations of RD and AxD effects, statistical significance maps for all metrics, and thorough harmonization evaluation showing ComBat successfully aligned bundle profiles while preserving diagnosis effects, though with some inflation in brainstem bundles. The study notes that while TBSS and other skeleton-based methods are more computationally efficient and have been used successfully in large-scale studies (e.g., ENIGMA-DTI), tractometry offers anatomically richer information when high-quality data and tractography are available.
